rules.rule: Test migrations on a Neon branch forked from production first, and run them on the main database only if the test is green.
Never merge develop into main automatically; only do so after the user explicitly asks.
Confirm the target branch before performing any merge.
When the user says "deploy" or "push," push only to the develop branch.
Merge to main only when the user explicitly says "merge to main" or "deploy to production."
Only switch the theme when the user issues an explicit /theme or /skin slash command; never switch it based on contextual keyword detection.
Do not call set_theme unless the user explicitly asks for it.
Before removing software judged "stale" (old Python interpreters, base Anaconda/Miniconda), check what depends on it before calling it safe to remove.
Keep Google Drive (FS) when cleaning up cloud sync software.
When dropping OneDrive, leave its files on disk and do not unlink them.
Write debloat scripts that run in dry-run mode first so the user can curate them, then execute them.
For each Python interpreter or distro slated for removal, check its Scripts directory for console scripts that point to it.
When clearing %TEMP%, exclude %TEMP%\claude, Claude Code's own task-output directory.
For each Python interpreter or distro slated for removal, grep profile and init files for its path.
Never label an interpreter or distro slated for removal as safe to remove without first running the dependents check.
Never modify or remove the remote-access stack (AnyDesk, Tailscale, SonicWall NetExtender, QuickAssist) when debloating the user's Windows desktop.
Never use git worktrees on this project.
Do not run git worktree remove --force unsupervised to clean up leftover worktrees; leave that to the user.
Never leave Playwright screenshot PNG files in the repository root.
Do NOT build Wave 3 stores without the cross-window sync layer.
Always check `git log --oneline -5` to confirm what is on main before cherry-picking.
Do not generate a new pack during a Playwright run; use the existing Cardboard.apg fixture instead.
Always check issue blockers before starting a phase of the ExSize project.
When the /tdd N command is invoked for issue N, check the project progress table to confirm that issue N's dependencies are met before starting work on it.
Only proceed to the next phase when every reviewer returns PASS.
Never paste real secret token values into memory files or plan docs.
Do not attempt a code fix for the Shopify private_access_tokens 401 error; it resolves on its own once the store goes live.
Do not fix the CORS error in the exchange-rate fetch (api.frankfurter.app blocked in lib/currency.ts/store/currencyStore.ts) until the user says to.
When creating a daily log, check the MEMORY.md index first.
When creating a daily log, read the June 18 log in the Client Requirements Checklist folder as a format reference.
Write the daily log to Client Requirements Checklist/DAILY_LOG_YYYY-MM-DD.md, using today's date.
Never run git push, git commit, git add, or any destructive git command.
After making code changes, stop at the file edits and do not proceed to any git operations.
Do not stage, commit, or push changes even if it seems like a natural next step.
Never put API keys, bearer tokens, secrets, or credentials in plan docs, spec docs, code files, or any markdown/documentation file.
Store secrets only in `.env.local` and Vercel environment variables, never in committed files.
If the 51k Brisk CRM lead list resurfaces, do not build import or send tooling for it without first re-confirming where the list came from.
Do not start the next build phase until the user has explicitly replied "Yes, Proceed."
Do not create a `tailwind.config.ts` file.
Do not reconnect acmevintagesupply.com in Shopify → Domains, because it overwrites GoDaddy DNS records.
When updating stock quantities for existing Shopify products, use bulk edit rather than a CSV import, to avoid creating duplicates.
Never store WordPress login credentials or passwords in memory files.
Before changing code in this project, diagnose the problem via debug instrumentation first.
After adding diagnostics, read the console or execute_code result before writing any code.
Only write fix code after the diagnostic results have been read.

Do not use the checkpoint joint_los15_az170.pt for cross-scene evaluation, because it was trained with a random split and leaks test UEs in a geo-split test; use the geo-split source model results/geo_split/100k/geo_geographic.pt instead.
When preparing a commit for JD-2207/CSI-ISAC, add new files only under `src/exp/*.py`.
Never stage `src/data` in a commit to JD-2207/CSI-ISAC.
Never stage `src/checkpoint` in a commit to JD-2207/CSI-ISAC.
Never stage `src/results` in a commit to JD-2207/CSI-ISAC.
